summary: Players race in real time to find the shortest path to slide a colored robot onto its target, with robots sliding until they hit a wall or another robot. It's a shared puzzle rather than a traditional turn-based game — everyone stares at the same board and shouts out solutions as they spot them.
praised: Simultaneous real-time play keeps everyone engaged, no downtime
Endlessly replayable due to random target/board setups
Great mental workout, satisfying aha-moment solutions
Works for a huge range of group sizes and ages
criticised: Can feel stressful or unfair to slower thinkers
Not really a 'game' in the traditional sense (no hidden info, negotiation, or asymmetry)
Loud/dominant players can shout out answers constantly, sidelining others
Little social interaction beyond competing to solve first
Can cause decision paralysis or frustration for some players

interaction.kind: simultaneous competitive puzzle-solving, no direct conflict

scoring.why: Whoever accumulates the most solved targets (found in fewest moves) across rounds wins
